name: Distrito Federal
summary_text: CDMX recorded the highest transfeminicide toll in the country in 2024 — 17 LGBT+ homicides, of which 11 were trans women — and remains among the highest-count states in 2025. The raw violence data is a negative signal for a visitor, though part of the elevated count reflects the city's superior reporting infrastructure rather than proportionally higher danger. Counterbalanced by the strongest institutional response of any Mexican state: transfeminicide made a distinct crime in July 2024 ("Ley Paola Buenrostro", the second state to do so); a dedicated Transfeminicide Investigation Unit created December 2024 covering all violent deaths of trans women; a prosecutor's protocol (Acuerdo FGJCDMX/04/2025) requiring feminist-context investigation with immediate-action deadlines (72h/48h); a new Gender Police launched August 2025 with 30 patrol units. Long-standing LGR since 2014, extended to 12-year-olds by 2021 decree. For a visitor assaulted in CDMX, there is trained machinery to investigate; in Nuevo León (0.40) or Michoacán (0.40) there is none. Modestly above the national 0.55: the protective and investigative framework is the strongest in Mexico and materially changes what a visitor who encounters violence or discrimination faces after the fact, even though the pre-violence risk data is the country's worst.

sources.claim_summary: Annual report (May 2025) by a Mexican LGBT+ news collective on homicides of LGBT+ people in Mexico in 2024: for the first time CDMX topped the national count with 17 homicides, 11 of them trans women, ahead of Nuevo León (5); 115 recorded violent incidents nationally, of which 59 killings. The primary state-by-state violence data.

NOTE: cached page returned only site navigation; the underlying CNN en Español report (19 July 2024) covers Mexico City's congress approving transfeminicide as a distinct crime in the penal code — the reform dubbed the "Ley Paola Buenrostro" after a trans woman murdered in 2016, making CDMX the second state to create the offence.
